a.hook: A is a worn-down form of one: Old English ān meant both one and a.

firstUse.source: c. 1589–1590 (date written), Christopher Marlo[we], edited by Tho[mas] Heywood, The Famous Tragedy of the Rich Iew of Malta. […], London: […] I[ohn] B[eale] for

relatives.note: the same word, kept at full strength
